newsitem.title: UK: LPC-British Energy loan raises 215 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: LPC-British Energy loan raises 215 mln stg.

text.p: LONDON, September 5 (LPC) - British Energy's 500 million stg credit has outstripped expectations by raising 215 million stg in general syndication, bankers said.
The deal's five arrangers -- BZW, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank, Industrial Bank of Japan, Midland Bank and the Royal Bank of Scotland -- had initially set a general syndication target of 75 million stg.

That amount would have allowed the five co-arrangers -- Bank of Nova Scotia, Banque Paribas, Societe Generale, Sumitomo Bank and Union Bank of Switzerland -- to be scaled back from their original underwriting commitment of 50 million stg to 35 million stg. Further scalebacks will be made accordingly.
"We're extremely delighted," said one arranger who preferred to remain anonymous.
When launched, the loan, for the newly-privatised British nuclear generator, was criticised by bankers who thought that the nuclear connection would make it a difficult deal to sell.
The credit is split between a 275 million stg revolver and a 225 million stg term loan, both with final maturities of five years.
Pricing on the revolver is 27.5 bps over LIBOR while the term loan has a margin of 35 bps.
